correctness.rationale: Exact group-algebra decomposition by m odd roots gives one Y-local algebra of length d per root. The X+X^-1 multiplier has precisely two size-M/2 nilpotent blocks; at root 1, Y+Y^-1 has local double zero, while at each other root its shift by the eigenvalue has a simple zero. A proven power-of-two tensor lemma yields a uniform set of zero-primary Jordan blocks plus an explicit uniform family of nonzero-primary Jordan blocks for each nontrivial root of unity. Dimensions add to the total number of torus cells. Nonzero Jordan powers have kernel dimension a minimum determined by the block length and the power-of-two part of the time exactly when the odd eigenvalue order divides the odd part of t; the gcd polynomial counts all relevant roots with no multiplicity. Möbius inversion and the Fitting decomposition give exact primitive periods and entry shells. A concrete script independently checked 224 pairs of binary-field power/fixed-point matrix nullities and every one of 4096 states on the four-by-three torus. Boundary cases d=1 and d>=M were checked algebraically, and finite experiments are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The full recurrent state portrait of a spatially periodic local parity system is a natural dynamical invariant. The result supplies exact temporal fixed-point counts, primitive orbit counts, maximum primitive period, and the joint distribution with time to the periodic component for an infinite mixed-circumference family. The strong and non-obvious split between fixed-state existence (3 divides the odd circumference) and genuine three-cycle existence (5 divides it) gives a structural arithmetic phase distinction. The uniform nonzero Jordan chain classification is not obtained by the prior zero-primary computation and is nontrivial even when no large numerical table is needed.
